title: Microburst incident deep-dive (perf sync)
body:
Meeting: Microburst incident deep-dive (perf sync)
Date: 2025-04-04
Attendees: Asha Kumar (owner), Jared Li, Camille Ortega, Ethan Park, Sofie Novak, oncall SRE (rotating)
Goal: Share reproduction runs, align on hypotheses for the sudden P95/P99 latency spikes observed 2025-04-03 02:00-05:00 UTC, agree next experiments and owners.

1) One-line summary
- Brief flurry of 200–600ms P99 spikes on hosted API for long-seq (>=1024) streaming requests under steady QPS. Baseline unaffected for short seq loads. Noted across two clusters (us-west-2-a, eu-central-1-b).

2) Timeline / how we discovered it
- 2025-04-03 02:12 UTC: anomaly triggered alarm (p99 > 700ms for model/long-seq).
- 02:15–02:35: automated fallback to smaller model variant engaged (reduced errors but user-visible latency).
- 03:00: SRE started capture of kernel traces + runtime logs; engineer ran targeted nightly harness reproduce.
- 04:20: first repro run succeeded locally (see run-id run-20250403-0418).

3) Test matrix we ran (high level)
- Model variants: redwood-7b, redwood-7b-8bit, redwood-13b-quant
- Hardware: A100-40GB (dedicated), T4 (hosted burst), V100 (legacy pool)
- Configs: seq_len=[256,512,1024,2048], batch_size=[1,4,8], streaming=true/false, kv_cache=true/false
- Load profile: steady QPS 40, 80, 160; artificial burst window (10s ramp)

4) Key numeric findings (representative)
- Baseline (control) redwood-7b, A100, seq=256, bs=4: p50=28ms, p95=82ms, p99=140ms at QPS=80.
- Regressed case redwood-7b, A100, seq=1024, bs=1, streaming:true: p50=180ms, p95=620ms, p99=950ms at QPS=40.
- With kv_cache disabled: p99 dropped ~40% (950ms -> 560ms) in same run (suggests cache handling implicated).
- T4 hosts show higher variance but similar pattern; V100 pool did not show consistent spike (lower traffic during window).

5) Observations from logs / traces
- Frequent small GC-like stalls inside the runtime slab allocator when seq > 1024 (heap walker shows repeated free/coalesce ops).
- KV cache eviction logs show synchronized eviction sweeps aligned to spike windows (eviction sweep duration 200–450ms).
- CUDA kernel stall traces show occasional 50–200ms queue stalls when multiple streams submit KV fetch + attention kernel concurrently.

6) Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1 (high confidence): KV cache eviction sweep becomes O(N) at higher prefixes and triggers blocking path in hot code. Evidence: eviction timestamps line up with p99 spikes; toggling kv_cache reduces the effect.
- H2 (medium): Combined kernel scheduling + stream contention on A100 at our concurrency pattern causes queuing delays for long sequences. Evidence: kernel traces show bursts; lower on V100.
- H3 (low): New allocator change in runtime PR #1284 (merged 2025-03-28) introduced lock contention under large-seq streaming. Evidence: timing correlates but repro without PR reverted not yet run.

7) Reproduction steps (short)
- Use repro harness: infra/bench/repro/run.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 1024 --streaming true --batch 1 --qps 40 --duration 10m --run-id run-20250403-0418
- Grab logs: s3://redwood-logs/serving/microburst/<run-id> and run grafana panel linked above.
- If unable to repro on hosted pool, spin dedicated A100 single-node with same docker image sha: sha256:4f3a2b.. and run harness.

8) Action items (owner + due)
- Asha: run targeted repro with allocator reverted (PR 1284 revert branch) and compare latency metrics. Due 2025-04-07.
- Jared: add fine-grained KV cache tracing (per-key timing + async eviction accounting) to runtime and ship to canary. Due 2025-04-08.
- Camille: schedule dedicated A100 repro node for evening window; collect CUDA queue-depth metrics and nvprof traces. Due 2025-04-06.
- Ethan: create small benchmark that reproduces eviction O(N) with synthetic prefixes; submit as unit-test / perf test. Due 2025-04-09.
- Sofie (SRE): keep fallback routing config active for long-seq routes and record customer impact metrics. Ongoing.

9) Short-term mitigations considered / performed
- Rollback of canary changes (not yet performed) — decision deferred until allocator repro fully validated.
- Temporary policy: route long-seq streaming traffic to dedicated nodes with kv_cache disabled during peak hours (requires config change; SRE to implement if tests confirm).

10) Unresolved questions
- Why does disabling kv_cache reduce p99 but not p50 proportionally? Is there a different hot path for fast requests?
- Is eviction sweep triggered by absolute memory pressure or a specific pattern (e.g., many different prefix keys)? Need per-key churn analysis.
- Does the allocator lock contention only surface with streaming=true? Repro tests needed for non-streaming long seq.

11) Next sync
- Follow-up perf sync scheduled: 2025-04-09 09:00 UTC (tentative). Expected attendees: owners above + runtime infra lead. Agenda: results of allocator revert + KV tracing.

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Captured a handful of shell snippets used in repro; stash to bench repo under /tmp/repro-snippets-20250403.txt (will move to infra/bench after cleaning).
- Quick checklist for PR review: focus on lock-free eviction handshake, avoid synchronous coalescing during streaming path.

References / attachments: see linked_artifacts above for Grafana, S3 logs, PR.

End of notes.
